issues.reason: ScienceDirect prefixes chapter titles with their chapter number in the HTML/metadata harvest ('Chapter 21 The financial accelerator...'), but 'Chapter 21' is a running header, not part of the title, and belongs (if anywhere) in the BibTeX 'chapter' field, not concatenated into 'title'.

Handbook of Macroeconomics Volume 1 (Taylor & Woodford, eds., 1999) was published as three separately bound parts, 1A/1B/1C, each with its own ISBN. This chapter's ISBN per CrossRef (9780444501585) matches Volume 1C specifically (Elsevier catalog: 'Handbook of Macroeconomics, Volume 1C', covering pp. 1231-1745), not 1A or 1B. Plain '1' is ambiguous/incomplete for this split volume.

@incollection requires 'booktitle' (the title of the book containing the chapter); the entry only had 'series', which is optional and does not substitute for the required field in standard BibTeX styles.

Taylor and Michael Woodford (confirmed via the Elsevier shop listing and multiple independent citations of this exact chapter). An @incollection entry conventionally carries the volume editor(s); the field was missing.

BibTeX hygiene: the 'doi' field should hold the bare DOI string, not a full resolver URL — the URL form belongs in (and is already duplicated by) the separate 'url' field. Most BibTeX/biblatex styles that print 'doi:...' prefixes will otherwise render 'doi:https://doi.org/...'.
BibTeX hygiene: a single hyphen renders as a hyphen, not an en dash; the convention (and what BibTeX/biblatex expects) is a double hyphen '--' to typeset as an en dash in a page range.
